subject: Issue getting/interpreting my parameter estimates (non-standardized vs standardized)

messages.author: d1b250b06cbb36a6
messages.subject: Issue getting/interpreting my parameter estimates (non-standardized vs standardized)
parts:
I would like to get non-standardized and standardized coefficient estimates for my SEM.
I have no latent variables, and I'm only specifying regressions ("~") and covariances only ("~~") in my model.
I'm getting the same estimate values for the columns "Estimate" and "Std.lv" (see example below). 

Are these non-standardized estimates?  As in, can I read that "one unit increase in B predicts a 0.206 unit increase in B"?
Or am I getting standardized values for my parameter estimates under "Estimates"? (As in, "one unit increase in B predicts 0.206 of a standard deviation increase in B"?)
The last column, Sdt.all reflects all standardized DVs and IVs, right? (As in, "one standard deviation increase in B predicts 0.169 of a standard deviation increased in B"?)

Thanks ahead of time!!

FitModel <- sem(Model, data = DataCaucNoRx, estimator = "MLR", likelihood = "wishart",fixed.x=FALSE)
summary (FitModel, standardized = T, fit.measures=T, rsquare=T)

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Issue getting/interpreting my parameter estimates (non-standardized vs standardized)
parts:
You are correct that the "Estimate" column is not standardized and the "Std.all" is standardized. The "Std.lv" column is the same as the "Estimate" column precisely because you have no factors in your model.
     The interpretation relates to change in A producing change in B--not change in B producing change in B.
